stands.name: The Kop
stands.description: The famous end behind the goal and home to Liverpool's most vocal supporters, known as 'Kopites'. Originally a vast terraced stand, it was rebuilt as an all-seater in 1994 and now incorporates safe-standing rail seating.

stands.name: Main Stand
stands.description: Expanded in 2016 with a towering third tier, making it one of the largest stands in European football. Houses the dressing rooms, press box, executive lounges and matchday hospitality.

stands.name: Anfield Road End
stands.description: Completed its major redevelopment in 2024, adding more than 7,000 seats across a new upper tier alongside modern concourse and hospitality spaces.

stands.name: Sir Kenny Dalglish Stand
stands.description: Named after Liverpool's greatest ever player. Opened in 1992 as the Centenary Stand, it was officially renamed in 2017 in honour of Sir Kenny Dalglish.

landmarks.name: This Is Anfield
landmarks.description: The iconic sign above the players' tunnel steps, installed by Bill Shankly to remind Liverpool players who they play for — and visiting teams who they are playing against.

landmarks.name: Shankly Gates
landmarks.description: The wrought-iron gates at Anfield Road, unveiled in 1982 in tribute to Bill Shankly and crowned with the words 'You'll Never Walk Alone'.

landmarks.name: The Hillsborough Memorial
landmarks.description: A permanent memorial honouring the 97 children, women and men who unlawfully lost their lives as a result of the Hillsborough disaster on 15 April 1989.

landmarks.name: The Paisley Gateway
landmarks.description: Erected in 1999 near the Kop entrance to celebrate the legacy of Bob Paisley, including the three European Cups won under his leadership.

foundingStory: Liverpool FC was born from a bitter dispute. In 1892, Everton FC left Anfield over a rent disagreement with stadium owner John Houlding. Left with an empty ground and no team, Houlding founded Liverpool Football Club on 15 March 1892. Admitted to the Football League the following year, Liverpool won their first league championship in 1901. What began with one man's resolve to keep football alive at Anfield grew into one of the most decorated and storied clubs in world sport.

traditions.name: You'll Never Walk Alone
traditions.description: Adopted by the Kop after Gerry and the Pacemakers took their cover to No. 1 in 1963, 'You'll Never Walk Alone' is sung before every home match at Anfield — an unmistakable symbol of the club's unity and resilience.

traditions.name: The Kop
traditions.description: Named in 1906 after Spion Kop, the South African hill where many soldiers from Merseyside regiments fell during the Boer War. For more than a century, the Kop has been the vocal heartbeat of Anfield.

traditions.name: The Boot Room
traditions.description: Originally a small storage room beneath Anfield where Bill Shankly and his coaches gathered over tea to dissect matches. The Boot Room shaped Liverpool's footballing culture and produced an unmatched managerial dynasty: Paisley, Fagan and Dalglish.

traditions.name: This Is Anfield
traditions.description: First hung in the tunnel by Bill Shankly in the 1970s, touching the 'This Is Anfield' frame on the walk to the pitch became a matchday ritual. Under Jürgen Klopp, players earned the right to touch it only after winning a major honour with the club.
